newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crop progress highlights - USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crop progress highlights - USDA.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Monday said one percent of the corn crop was very poor, four percent poor, 22 percent fair, 56 percent in good and 17 percent excellent.
Among the 17 major corn-producing states, seven percent of the corn crop had silked, compared to 11 percent one year ago and a five-year average of 15 percent, USDA said.
The U.S. soybean crop was rated one percent very poor, six percent poor, 27 percent fair, 55 percent good and 11 percent excellent, USDA said.
USDA said 23 percent of the soybean crop was blooming, compared to 16 percent one year ago and a five-year average of 23 percent.
The department said two percent of the cotton crop was very poor, eight percent poor, 30 percent fair, 47 percent good and 13 percent excellent.
In spring wheat fields, three percent was rated very poor, 15 percent was poor, 32 percent was fair, 45 percent was good and five percent was excellent, USDA said.
Some 63 percent of the winter wheat crop was harvested, compared to 61 percent one year ago and a five-year average of 60 percent, USDA said.
